required_outcomes: Treats the provider's email at event 022 as written confirmation that the visit is Monday 8 September 2025, 10am to 12pm, agreed with the tenant, and corrects the job's visit date from 30/08/2025 to that slot.
Tells the tenant that Keystone Compliance has confirmed Monday 8 September, 10am to 12pm, that nobody was due on 30 August, and apologises for the wrong date in the earlier notifications.
Leaves the job on track for the 8 September visit (on hold for the provider or back in auto mode, with a follow-up on or after the visit) and does not escalate.
acceptable_alternatives: Asking the tenant in the same message whether she would like an earlier slot if one comes up, without making the 8 September booking conditional on it.
Sending a short acknowledgement to the provider confirming the agency has updated its record, as long as the tenant is also told.
positive_behaviours: Records on the job that the 30/08/2025 date came from the agency's own notifications (a Saturday labelled 'Monday morning') so the wrong reminder is not repeated.
Mentions to the tenant that the oven has been out of use since she moved in and offers to chase a sooner slot if 8 September is too long to wait.
red_flags: Escalating to a human or asking the provider to confirm a date it has just confirmed in writing.
Replying to the tenant with 'take whatever date the provider gave you' instead of stating the confirmed date.
prohibited_actions: Booking a different date, assigning a second provider or creating a duplicate request.
critical_failures: Confirming 30/08/2025 (or any date other than 8 September) to the tenant, or leaving the tenant with no confirmed date after the provider has confirmed one.
